scope: Independent methods and source-transcription review of the Round 14 ruxolitinib cream HS audit; not a reconstruction of clinical analyses or a new HHD efficacy assessment.

source_checks.access: Independently read public SAP text before reviewing authored files; subsequently verified the downloaded PDF hash and viewed actual local rendered page images.
Independently read root-downloaded exact official JSON, with matching bytes and SHA-256.

source_checks.locators: Primary result, secondary endpoint bullets, symptoms, adverse events and trial population paragraphs

source_checks.access: Indexed journal excerpts were supplied by root and author; this reviewer did not independently read the full journal article, supplement or complete protocol. Main numerical result checks use C1 and R1.

checks.finding: Strict JSON parsing found no duplicate keys. Seventeen distinct result rows map to all eleven posted registry outcome objects, with source identities preserved.

Randomized and safety arm counts are 34/35. Lesion endpoint displays use 24/32 and pain/itch displays 23/22. Full longitudinal model-contributing counts remain unknown; the audit does not substitute displayed N for those counts.

Primary means, standard errors, reported difference -1.20, 95% interval [-2.21,-0.18] and P=.0215 match registry fields. The reported coefficient is preserved rather than replacing it with subtraction of rounded means.

Adjusted pain, itch, IHS4 and pre-existing-area AN values, uncertainty and displayed denominators match the registry. Sponsor symptom/IHS4 figures remain separate and their unspecified estimators are not declared to be raw means.
Responder percentages and directly reported denominators match source fields. Missing response numerators remain null; no percentage inversion or all-randomized nonresponder analysis is invented.

Controlled-period flow is 34/35 started, 24/32 completed and 10/3 not completed. Extension flow is 24/32 started, 21/24 completed and 3/8 not completed. Every reported noncompletion reason reconciles to the period total; reasons are not assigned to individual missing outcomes.
The SAP distinguishes randomized ITT, application-based safety, planned MMRM and exploratory alpha .10. The audit correctly notes that P=.0215 also meets .05; no HHD sample size follows.

The seven-day symptom diary rule makes the visit score missing when at least four daily values are missing. No explicit MAR/MNAR, categorical imputation or sensitivity algorithm is inferred from the model name or redactions.

MMRM narrative versus ANCOVA structured method fields remains unresolved for all five continuous outcomes. Planned SAP inclusion, available-data registry labels and verified implementation are kept distinct.

DBVC TEAEs in 13/34 versus 15/35 participants and grade ≥3 events in 0/34 versus 2/35 are accurate. Extension safety uses 24/32 denominators with both groups on active treatment. Pooled serious-event totals of 2/66 active-exposed and 1/35 vehicle-exposed are not presented as a randomized safety comparison.
The extension adds 16 weeks through week 32. Both origin groups receive active cream; the audit does not infer a continued active-versus-vehicle maintenance effect or drug-free durability.

No HHD efficacy, exposure clearance, symptom failure, equivalence, new effect threshold or independent replication is claimed. Symptom intervals are interpreted as uncertain; overlapping lesion measures do not establish pain benefit.

review_cycle_updates: The initial draft preceded successful recovery of the official registry JSON. Final files incorporate its actual denominators, confidence intervals, participant flow and safety windows.
Actual local page-image inspection replaced insufficient web screenshot placeholders before the visual redaction claim was accepted.
remaining_evidence_limits: The exact participants and visits contributing to each fitted model, daily diary missingness, implemented imputation and missing-outcome sensitivity results remain unverified.

The SAP p25 parenthetical concerning new ANs in the pre-existing-area endpoint is potentially ambiguous. Registry outcome 2 explicitly includes new lesions in baseline-affected areas and excludes newly affected areas; R13 accurately attributes that scope to the registry. These SAP and registry descriptions are not independently reconciled.
Baseline symptom and BSA distributions, measured HS plasma exposure and detailed extension efficacy are not recovered.
The full manuscript, supplement, full protocol and individual-participant data were not independently reviewed; this verdict concerns the bounded audit and its stated source limits.
